quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area
The highest or lowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
The speed you should drive in heavy traffic
The speed you should drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest safe speed allowed on the road. The maximum speed is for good conditions. You must drive slower when conditions are bad.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually to a stop.
Keep driving as normal.
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly if a tire blows out. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Let off the gas slowly to reduce speed. Once you are going very slow, tap the brakes lightly and move off the road to a safe spot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road ahead.
No parking.
Right lane is closed.
Many turns ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about road hazards ahead. This sign warns that the road curves ahead. Slow down and adjust your speed.

questions.question: What does this road sign show?

options.text: The safe speed for a residential area.
The safe speed for leaving a highway.
The safe speed for entering a highway.
The safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The safe speed for leaving a highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the recommended safe speed for highway exits. In this example, it shows 30 mph.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When leaving a highway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your distance behind another vehicle when: a large vehicle blocks your view, the weather is bad, traffic is heavy, you are leaving a highway, you are behind a motorcycle or bicycle, or someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: A driver extends their left arm downward. What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turning left.
Turning right.
Stopping.
Starting up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping.
questions.explanation: A left arm pointing downward means the driver is going to stop. Adjust your driving if you see this signal from the driver ahead.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: It can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
It has a triangular shape.
It is blue with black letters.
It shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Signs with recommended speeds suggest how fast to drive on curves and turns. Even if you feel safe driving faster in good weather, never exceed the recommended speed in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: What helps direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning on some highways?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the road edge
White arrows painted in the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows painted in the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows painted on the road show which lanes to use. They direct drivers to turn or go straight as needed.

questions.question: A green arrow changes to a solid green light. What can you do?

options.text: You may turn, but yield to oncoming traffic.
You cannot turn and must go straight.
You still have the right to turn.
You no longer need to turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn, but yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction. However, you must first let pedestrians and oncoming cars pass safely.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and drive in front of them.
Stop and let them cross safely.
Drive close to scare them so they will not cross illegally again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians and cars in an intersection, even when you have a green light. Pedestrian safety is your top priority.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your reaction time.
The time of day.
Your vehicle's brake condition.
Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed. The time of day does not affect it.

questions.question: You cannot park:

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the curb.

questions.question: When a transit bus signals to return to the road after a stop, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any transit bus that is signaling to return to the road. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus enter traffic safely.

questions.question: When you turn right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Yield to pedestrians.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You may turn right on a green light unless a sign says otherwise. When turning, you must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle's signal. You should:

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are open for the emergency vehicle.
Stop immediately.
Slow down, move to create a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to create a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, slow down and create a clear path for the emergency vehicle. Stop and do not try to drive faster than it.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, reduce speed, and drive to a safe area to stop.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, reduce speed, and drive to a safe area to stop.
questions.explanation: If power steering fails, steering will require more effort. Reduce your speed and pull off the road to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between lanes is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross broken white lines to pass if the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: You can reduce hydroplaning risk by driving:

options.text: Through shallow water.
Faster.
Slower.
Through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down to reduce the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Intersection ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is coming from both directions ahead.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Build good habits when entering your car. Before starting the engine, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
A circular intersection is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
These lanes are for buses and carpools with a driver and at least one passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that these parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection. The light is green but there is heavy oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection instead.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn because you have a green light and have the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: You may enter the intersection to prepare for your left turn when the light is green. Wait in the center of the intersection for oncoming traffic to pass before you turn.

questions.question: You are in an accident and someone is injured. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Never move the injured person.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless you must. Moving them carelessly can make injuries worse. Keep the injured person warm while you wait for help. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves are ahead.
A divided highway is starting.
A divided highway is ending.
There are bumps in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is ending.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the divided highway will end ahead.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are just suggestions.
Must be followed only when other traffic is present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must always be obeyed.
questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: When driving through curves, the most important thing is:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before entering the curve.
Speed up slightly before entering the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle may slide if you go too fast through a curve. Slow down before you enter the curve to keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: A driver taking a non-prescription drug should:

options.text: Read the drug labels before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Drive normally even if there are warning labels.
Drive only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the drug labels before driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving. Check the label for warnings before driving. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist.

questions.question: You find a problem with your vehicle that may affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have money.
Drive at slower speeds.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any problem that could affect safe driving right away. Do not drive the vehicle until it is fixed.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the freeway shoulder?

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except during an emergency.

questions.question: You see a "Merging traffic" sign on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Honk at the incoming traffic.
Keep driving at your current speed.
Speed up to avoid congestion.
Change lanes if safe to let traffic merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes if safe to let traffic merge.
questions.explanation: When traffic is merging, move to another lane if it is safe to do so. This helps traffic enter smoothly.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching you on a one-way street. What must you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until it passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Keep your tires properly inflated.
Slow down when driving in rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep tire tread in good condition, maintain proper tire pressure, and reduce speed in rain. Hydroplaning happens more often at higher speeds.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol reduce your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. You cannot drive safely after drinking.

questions.question: When may you turn right on red?

options.text: When there is a sign prohibiting the turn.
Before pedestrians have crossed the intersection.
After you stop completely and yield to pedestrians and other vehicles.
Before coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you stop completely and yield to pedestrians and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: You may turn right on red only after coming to a full stop. Check that there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Make sure it is safe and watch for pedestrians.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs mark railroad crossings. Yield to trains and do not try to drive across the tracks before a train passes.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with drugs?

options.text: The effects decrease.
The effects of both increase.
It helps cure illness.
It improves your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both increase.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can increase the effects of both. This makes driving very dangerous. Never drive after consuming alcohol or drugs, and especially not after using both together.

questions.question: You are driving behind a school bus with flashing red lights. What must you do?

options.text: Stop at least 25 feet away.
Slow down to 10 mph.
Speed up and pass.
Stop directly behind the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at least 25 feet away.
questions.explanation: When a school bus shows flashing red lights, stop at least 25 feet away. The only exception is on a divided highway when the bus is on the opposite side—then slow to 10 mph.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to get drivers to let you through.
Drive around a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. This way, if a car hits you from behind, you will not be pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When may you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen because drivers do unexpected things. You should let other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know your plans. Use your turn signals when slowing down, stopping, or changing direction. Use your emergency signals or horn when needed.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign:

options.text: Be ready to drive faster than the train.
Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and continue driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs warn drivers that a train might be coming. Always obey these signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning sign.

questions.question: Before turning left, it is important to:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Yield to oncoming vehicles.
Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic light, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: White
Red
Black
Yellow

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When approaching a curve in the roadway, drivers should slow down:

options.text: Before entering the curve.
After completing the curve.
In the middle of the curve.
Only if they see approaching traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Driving too fast through a curve can cause your tires to lose grip on the road.

questions.question: While driving, your wheels slip off the edge of the road. You should:

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Slow down by gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, keep them off the pavement and slow down gently with the brakes. Once you are going slow enough, turn the steering wheel to get back onto the pavement. Do not jerk the steering wheel suddenly.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Inattentive driving
Excessive speed under the driving conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Driving too fast for conditions causes many crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, you:

options.text: May not exit the freeway.
May either continue through the interchange or exit the freeway from your current lane.
May stay in your lane and continue through the interchange.
Must exit the freeway, if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must exit the freeway, if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means your lane does not continue on the highway. It will only go off the highway as an exit ramp. If you are in this lane, you can change lanes to stay on the highway, or you must exit.

questions.question: If you are driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give a motorcycle driver a full lane width. Even if there seems to be room to share a lane, the motorcycle needs space to move safely.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. You should:

options.text: Speed up and get through the intersection.
Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Wait for that vehicle to safely pass before you go.
